items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Red Nichols and HIIs Five Pennies

ctx.x: MR. JOHNSON: So the only thing I could never play was the bass and the piano. But anyway, by this time we had augmented the band, and we changed the name of the band to the Blue Moon Chasers. And actually, this was a good band. Man, the two of us really began to start in the summer time, and I can remember just as well, on one of my first tours --

See, I -- we had been listening to every band that come into Dallas. We would go and hear them, and stand up in front of the band and just absorb all of the music we could, and we'd go back and try to imitate whatever good we thought was there, and incidentally, by the same token, we were copying records, like Red Nichols and HIIs Five Pennies; copying Coleman Hawkins solos off the record there; Fletcher Henderson, and some of Louie Armstrong, ~~we~~ he'd started recording for Okeh Records, and we would copy his…

We Would copy anybody's solo that was good, and I don't care whether it was a piano, or ~~want~~ you, know, we would try to copy this. Well actually, all of this was really a school, because, you know, you're copying off of a record, you're really developing an ear. It's -- and pitch, and you're learning how -- we wasn't writing it down, though. All of this would just play this over and over and over till we could hum the solos, and when we could hum the solos, then we would find it on our instruments, you see?…
